extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedy writers, comedy mentors, comedy fans, and anyone who needs to be funnier in speeches or performances
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide to creating and refining jokes using repeatable elements and a dependable writing process that applies across comedic genres (stand-up, sitcom, satire, prose, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal organization of a joke — how set-up and punchline (and other structural parts) are arranged to produce laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kalan lists Structure as a core element of all jokes and devotes a chapter to it; he advises tending joke structure as part of the farming metaphor (planting, tending, harvesting) to make material reliably funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: The central idea or conceit that a joke is built on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book identifies Premise as a foundational element and uses the imagery of 'plant[ing] their premises' — emphasizing generating strong, clear premises as the seed of a joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer/performer’s distinctive personality or perspective as expressed in comedic material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice is named explicitly as one of the key elements; guidance implies shaping material to fit a consistent, recognizable voice appropriate to the performer and genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The attitude or mood conveyed by the joke (e.g., biting, playful, ironic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone is listed as a separate element and treated as something to manage so jokes land as intended for the audience and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording / Word Choice / Vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise choice of words and vocabulary that make a line funny or memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jacket copy highlights 'hilarious word choice' and reviewers call out 'vocabulary' — the book analyzes phrasing and precise language choices that yield laughs; wording is a chapter topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and writing for the specific audience who will hear or read the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience is one of the named elements and gets a chapter; the book emphasizes tailoring material to 'whoever they may be' (from wedding guests to viewers of a show).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrasing and Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: The cadence, timing of words, and how lines are phrased to create comedic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kalan analyzes 'phrasing, rhythm, and precise details' from examples in his career and others' work, showing how rhythm and phrasing contribute to punch and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific, concrete details chosen to sharpen a joke and make it more vivid/funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description notes 'the phrasing, rhythm, and precise details that make their work so dang funny' — advising careful selection of concrete details to elevate humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatable Process / Method
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependable, repeated workflow for generating and developing jokes rather than waiting for inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central thesis: 'it’s easier to write jokes when you have a dependable method' — described metaphorically as a farm: plant premises, tend structure and wording, harvest material; this process 'lessens stress and agony and yields more reliable rewards.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rewriting and Iteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive revision of lines and bits until they reach maximum funny — iterative polishing is part of craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kalan shows examples of jokes he 'wrote (and rewrote and rewrote and rewrote . . . )' and the book promises 'repeatable steps that can be followed to take an idea to a fully formed gut buster,' signaling heavy emphasis on revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability Across Genres / Adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to apply the same comedic elements and methods to different formats (stand-up, sitcoms, satire, prose, children's comedy, visual humor, podcasting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The jacket states the elements 'can be applied to any comedic genre' and the table of contents includes chapters on multiple genres, indicating guidance on adapting core elements to each medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The moment-to-moment placement of beats and pauses that determine when a laugh occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers single out 'timing' as a focus area; combined with the book's attention to phrasing and rhythm, timing is treated as a craft skill to be learned and applied.
